messages:
maria: FYI - onboarding ZephyrX->Qwen-lite variant (fresh convert) and seeing consistent embed projection misalignment after int4 quant. Repro steps and minimal logs below.

alek: Can you paste the exact commands and a tiny sample of the bad outputs?

maria: repro (conda env + our convert tool):
```
# convert + quantize
python convert_model.py --src zephyrx-13b --tgt qwen-lite --export-format pt --preserve-vocab
python quantize.py --model qwen-lite.pt --bits 4 --scheme per-channel
# run a short eval
python eval_embeddings.py --model qwen-lite-int4.pt --input "The capital of France is"
```

maria: sample outputs (embedding cosine to fp16 baseline):
- fp16: baseline embedding vector (first 8 dims): [0.123, -0.045, 0.87, 0.002, ...]
- int4: produced vector (first 8 dims): [0.421, -0.221, -0.34, 0.112, ...]
- cosine(fp16, int4) = 0.37 (expected > 0.9 for this seed/sentence)

cheng: hmmm. That low cosine smells like either a head-order or proj-matrix transpose mismatch during export/quant. Did you check headwise projection layout (kqv/proj order) and rotary scale/freq parameters?

maria: I ran a quick diff on the state dict names. Layout looks consistent but discovered an odd per-head multiplier baked into the fp16 checkpoint: key `rotary.freq_scale` = 0.997. Converted model ended up with `rotary.freq_scale` = 1.0 after conversion. Could that cause such large drift?

riley: 0.003 delta seems small to cause cos=0.37. Are you sure tokenization mapping is identical? Mismatched BOS/EOS or an extra sentinel can flip embeddings heavily for short prompts. Try run embedding on longer prompts to check.

maria: tried longer prompt (200 tokens) - cosine still ~0.42. So not just BOS. I also dumped kv-cache headwise norms for the first token, normals are way off between fp16/int4.

alek: can you run a forward with single-layer isolated (same weights) in fp16 vs quantized kernel to see if difference arises pre-rotary? Put a breakpoint after proj matmul but before rotary application.

maria: did that. Snapshots (layer 4, first head):
- w.x (fp16, first 6 dims): [1.23, -0.11, 0.55, 0.02, 0.00, -0.03]
- w.x (int4, first 6 dims): [1.20, -0.10, 0.57, 0.01, 0.01, -0.02]
- After rotary in fp16: [0.9, -0.34, 0.67, ...]
- After rotary in int4: [0.03, -0.77, -0.41, ...]
So something in the rotary application is flipping phase/sign in int4 path.

cheng: That looks like an index/mapping error when constructing the sin/cos tables for fractional head dims. Qwen-lite conversion uses fractional head size (head_dim=64.0 but stored as 63 in some places) — could be an off-by-one when building the per-head table. I remember a similar subtle bug where the FFT-ish phase array used `np.linspace(0, d/2 - 1)` vs `0..d/2`.

riley: also check the ordering of the interleaved even/odd dims. Our runtime assumes [e0,o0,e1,o1,...] but some converters produce contiguous [e0,e1,...,o0,o1,...]. If int4 kernel packs differently, that would manifest exactly as phase-flipped-looking vectors.

maria: good point. I dumped the layout mask coming out of convert tool: converter emits `proj_layout=interleaved` but quant kernel unpacker expects `proj_layout=contiguous`.

alek: bingo. So conversion metadata mismatch. Two paths: change converter to emit contiguous or teach quant kernel to accept both. Which is faster to test?

cheng: quick patch on quant kernel walker to check header flag and branch on layout. I whipped up a small shim:
```
# naive shim in quant_unpacker.py
if header['proj_layout'] == 'interleaved':
    weights = deinterleave(weights)
# else leave as-is
```

maria: applied shim locally, re-ran eval: cosine(fp16,int4) = 0.91 now. Good sign. Generation quality looks aligned on short LM tests.

eval-bot: ALERT: automated eval-suite "embed-regressions" triggered - previous run (fp16) score 0.873 -> current int4 0.869 (delta -0.004). Within tolerance but flagged because of config change. See /eval/reports/8005001234.

riley: nice. We should still add a conversion test asserting `proj_layout` header is present and consistent. Also add a compat fallback in runtime but we should not rely on shim forever.

alek: agree. Please open a small PR: 1) make converter explicitly set `proj_layout` in metadata, 2) add test to conversion CI that rounds trip convert->quant->fp16 compare cosine on a couple prompts >0.9, 3) add brief note in release log.

maria: opened draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/models/pull/482 (title: "zephyrx->qwen: export proj_layout metadata + compat test"). Patch is minimal: set header, add test that uses our tiny sample.

maria: going to run full smoke on dedicated (dedicated-24g pool) to ensure perf/regressions on latency. Will report back.

alek: after smoke, let's also run eval-bench with and without rotary scaling (use env ROTARY_SCALE_OVERRIDE=1.0/0.997) to confirm no lingering scaling mismatch.

maria: ran smoke on dedicated: latency 5% higher on int4 (expected) but no correctness regressions. Also ran the two eval-bench configs - no diff when header fixed.

riley: great. Next steps: merge the converter header PR, add runtime fallback for a couple releases, and coordinate with infra to re-run nightly onboard-suite for all Qwen variants.

maria: logging the incident in onboarding tracker and marking owner @maria for follow-up. Thanks all :thumbsup:
